'''Jillian Lee Dempsey''' is an American [[Inorganic chemistry|inorganic chemist]] and the Bowman and Gordon Gray Distinguished Term Professor at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]]. Currently, her work focuses on [[proton-coupled electron transfer]], [[Electron transfer|charge transfer]] events, and [[quantum dots]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://dempsey.web.unc.edu/research/|title=Research – Dempsey Group|website=University of North Carolina|language=en-US|access-date=2018-04-26}}</ref> She is the recipient of numerous awards for rising stars of chemistry, including most recently a 2016 [[Sloan Fellowship|Alfred P. Sloan Research Fellowship]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://sloan.org/past-fellows|title=Past Fellows|website=sloan.org|access-date=2018-04-26|archive-date=2018-03-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180314000756/https://sloan.org/past-fellows}}</ref> and a 2016 [[United States Air Force|Air Force]]'s Young Investigator Research Program (YIP).<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://dau.dodlive.mil/2016/06/01/air-force-office-of-scientific-research-awards-grants-to-56-scientists-and-engineers-through-young-investigator-research-program-2/|title=Air Force Office of Scientific Research Awards Grants to 56 Scientists and Engineers through Young Investigator Research Program|date=2016-01-14|website=Defense Acquisition University|language=en-US|access-date=2018-04-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180427045149/http://dau.dodlive.mil/2016/06/01/air-force-office-of-scientific-research-awards-grants-to-56-scientists-and-engineers-through-young-investigator-research-program-2/|archive-date=2018-04-27}}</ref>

== Education and training ==
Dempsey attended the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] for her undergraduate, earning her S.B. in Chemistry in 2005. She worked with Prof. [[Daniel G. Nocera]] on the development of molecular [[water splitting]] catalysts.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Dempsey|first1=Jillian L.|last2=Esswein|first2=Arthur J.|last3=Manke|first3=David R.|last4=Rosenthal|first4=Joel|last5=Soper|first5=Jake D.|last6=Nocera|first6=Daniel G.|date=2005-10-01|title=Molecular Chemistry of Consequence to Renewable Energy|journal=Inorganic Chemistry|volume=44|issue=20|pages=6879–6892|doi=10.1021/ic0509276|pmid=16180843 |issn=0020-1669}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Esswein|first1=Arthur J.|last2=Dempsey|first2=Jillian L.|last3=Nocera|first3=Daniel G.|date=2007-04-01|title=A RhII−AuII Bimetallic Core with a Direct Metal−Metal Bond|journal=Inorganic Chemistry|volume=46|issue=7|pages=2362–2364|doi=10.1021/ic062203f|pmid=17326627 |issn=0020-1669}}</ref> While at MIT, she also worked at [[Merck Research Laboratories]]' Department of [[Analytical chemistry|Analytical Research]], on the development of [[HPLC]] columns for pharmaceutical [[Process chemistry|process development]].<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2004-10-11|title=Practical aspects of fast HPLC separations for pharmaceutical process development using monolithic columns|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0003267004010153|journal=Analytica Chimica Acta|language=en|volume=523|issue=2|pages=149–156|doi=10.1016/j.aca.2004.07.069|issn=0003-2670|last1=Wu |first1=Naijun |last2=Dempsey |first2=Jillian |last3=Yehl |first3=Peter M. |last4=Dovletoglou |first4=Angelos |last5=Ellison |first5=Dean |last6=Wyvratt |first6=Jean |bibcode=2004AcAC..523..149W |url-access=subscription }}</ref> Dempsey then travelled to the [[California Institute of Technology]] for graduate studies, where she worked in the laboratory of Prof. [[Harry B. Gray]] and [[Jay R. Winkler]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Dempsey|first1=Jillian L.|last2=Winkler|first2=Jay R.|last3=Gray|first3=Harry B.|date=2010-12-08|title=Proton-Coupled Electron Flow in Protein Redox Machines|journal=Chemical Reviews|volume=110|issue=12|pages=7024–7039|doi=10.1021/cr100182b|issn=0009-2665|pmc=3005815|pmid=21082865}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Dempsey|first1=Jillian L.|last2=Brunschwig|first2=Bruce S.|last3=Winkler|first3=Jay R.|last4=Gray|first4=Harry B.|date=2009-12-21|title=Hydrogen Evolution Catalyzed by Cobaloximes|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/full/10.1021/ar900253e|journal=Accounts of Chemical Research|volume=42|issue=12|pages=1995–2004|doi=10.1021/ar900253e|pmid=19928840 |bibcode=2009AcChR..42.1995D |issn=0001-4842|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Dempsey's research at Caltech focused on elucidating the mechanism of [[Water splitting|hydrogen evolution]] for [[cobaloxime]] catalysts,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Dempsey|first1=Jillian L.|last2=Winkler|first2=Jay R.|last3=Gray|first3=Harry B.|date=2010-01-27|title=Kinetics of Electron Transfer Reactions of H2-Evolving Cobalt Diglyoxime Catalysts|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=132|issue=3|pages=1060–1065|doi=10.1021/ja9080259|pmid=20043639 |bibcode=2010JAChS.132.1060D |issn=0002-7863}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Dempsey|first1=Jillian L.|last2=Winkler|first2=Jay R.|last3=Gray|first3=Harry B.|date=2010-12-01|title=Mechanism of H2 Evolution from a Photogenerated Hydridocobaloxime|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=132|issue=47|pages=16774–16776|doi=10.1021/ja109351h|pmid=21067158 |bibcode=2010JAChS.13216774D |issn=0002-7863}}</ref> as well as the reactivity of [[Photolysis|photogenerated]] osmium(II) complexes.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Dempsey|first1=Jillian L.|last2=Winkler|first2=Jay R.|last3=Gray|first3=Harry B.|date=2011-10-05|title=Redox reactivity of photogenerated osmium(II) complexes|url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2011/dt/c1dt11138h|journal=Dalton Transactions|language=en|volume=40|issue=40|pages=10633–10636|doi=10.1039/C1DT11138H|pmid=21892445 |issn=1477-9234|url-access=subscription}}</ref> She graduated with her Ph.D. in 2011.

From 2011 to 2012, Dempsey then conducted postdoctoral research as an NSF American Competitiveness in Chemistry Fellow in the laboratory of [[Daniel R. Gamelin]] at the [[University of Washington]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://depts.washington.edu/gmrg/people.html#alumni|title=Gamelin Research Group|website=University of Washington|access-date=2018-04-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180427044822/http://depts.washington.edu/gmrg/people.html#alumni|archive-date=2018-04-27}}</ref> There, she worked on photoconductive quantum dot thin films,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=White|first1=Michael A.|last2=Dempsey|first2=Jillian L.|last3=Carroll|first3=Gerard M.|last4=Gallagher|first4=James D.|last5=Gamelin|first5=Daniel R.|date=2013-09-01|title=Photoconductive ZnO films with embedded quantum dot or ruthenium dye sensitizers|journal=APL Materials|volume=1|issue=3|page=032107|doi=10.1063/1.4820428|doi-access=free|bibcode=2013APLM....1c2107W }}</ref> as well as magnetic coupling in illuminated quantum dots.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bradshaw|first1=Liam R.|last2=May|first2=Joseph W.|last3=Dempsey|first3=Jillian L.|last4=Li|first4=Xiaosong|last5=Gamelin|first5=Daniel R.|date=2014-03-19|title=Ferromagnetic excited-state Mn${}^{2+}$ dimers in Zn${}_{1\ensuremath{-}x}$MnxSe quantum dots observed by time-resolved magnetophotoluminescence |journal=Physical Review B|volume=89|issue=11|article-number=115312|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.89.115312}}</ref>

== Independent career ==
Dempsey began her independent career at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] in 2012 as an assistant professor. She was granted tenure in 2018 and promoted to the rank of associate professor. Since 2020, she has served as the Bowman and Gordon Gray Distinguished Term Professor.
